data.description:
## Problem

`MainThreadHangMonitor.appendToLog` (Sources/MainThreadHangMonitor.swift, ~line 669) appends every `hang.begin` / `hang.persist` / `hang.end` capture to `~/Library/Logs/c11/hang.log` (or `/tmp/c11-debug-<tag>-hang.log` for tagged builds, or `$C11_HANG_LOG`) with no cap and no rotation. A persist capture is a 96-frame symbolicated backtrace every 5 s, and during a sustained stall the C11-209 delegator measured ~23 MB/min (~1.3 GB/hr). On this machine `~/Library/Logs/c11/hang.log.wedged-20260911` is 238 MB from a single wedge. Nothing prunes it; a multi-hour stall on a shipped install eats the operator's disk.

Found by the C11-209 delegator; explicitly out of scope there.

## Fix

Cap the log with rotation, cheaply, on the watchdog thread (which is where `appendToLog` already runs):

- Track bytes written since process start plus one `stat` on first open; do not `stat` on every append.
- When the file would exceed a cap (suggest 32 MB), rotate: `hang.log` -> `hang.log.1`, keeping at most 2 archived generations (`hang.log.1`, `hang.log.2`), oldest deleted. Rotation happens at an episode boundary where possible (`hang.end`) so a single episode's timeline is not split; but a single episode that exceeds the cap on its own must still rotate mid-episode. Write a one-line `=== c11 hang.rotated <ts> ===` header at the top of the new file that says the previous file was rotated.
- Total on-disk footprint must stay under roughly 3x the cap.
- No allocation inside the `thread_suspend` / `thread_resume` window (there is none today because `appendToLog` runs after resume; keep it that way).
- Rotation must never run on the main thread and must never throw or trap; if rename fails, truncate.

## Tests

Pure-logic tests in `c11LogicTests`: factor the size/rotation decision into a testable seam (e.g. a small `HangLogRotator` struct that takes a path + cap and exposes `appendAndRotateIfNeeded`), then test: writes under cap do not rotate; crossing the cap rotates once; generations shift and the oldest is deleted; footprint bound holds after many rotations. Use a temp directory. No source-text or plist assertions.

## Validation

CI is the gate. Do NOT run `xcodebuild` locally on this machine (one build per machine rule; another build may hold the lock). Push the branch, open the PR, watch `gh pr checks`, iterate until green.
data.title: hang.log has no rotation or size cap: ~23 MB/min during a stall, 238 MB observed

data.body:
Plan (delegator, worktree agent-a97664689382fd4d6, branch c11-220-hang-log-rotation):

1. Add `struct HangLogRotator` at the bottom of Sources/MainThreadHangMonitor.swift. State: logURL, capBytes (32 MiB = 33554432), generations (2), a tracked size (Int?) that is probed exactly once via an injectable sizeProbe and thereafter maintained from FileHandle.seekToEnd() + bytes written. No stat per append.
2. append(_:episodeBoundary:) rules:
   - hard: if trackedSize + data.count > cap, rotate BEFORE writing (mid-episode rotation for a single oversized episode);
   - soft: on an episode boundary (hang.end) with trackedSize >= 75% of cap, write the closing record first, THEN rotate, so an episode timeline is never split;
   - otherwise plain append.
3. rotate(): delete <log>.2, shift <log>.1 -> <log>.2, move <log> -> <log>.1 (a pre-existing file already larger than the cap is deleted rather than archived, so the 238 MB legacy log cannot survive as an archive); on rename failure truncate <log> in place. Then write a one-line `=== c11 hang.rotated <ts> previous=... capBytes=... ===` header at the top of the new file. Never throws, never traps, runs on the watchdog thread only (same thread appendToLog already runs on), zero work inside the thread_suspend window.
   Footprint bound: current <= cap, two archives <= cap each => ~3x cap (96 MB).
4. Wire MainThreadHangMonitor to hold a `var hangLog: HangLogRotator`; handleHang passes episodeBoundary: false, handleRecovery passes true.
5. Tests: new c11Tests/HangLogRotatorTests.swift added to the c11LogicTests target (hand-edited pbxproj, new 24-hex IDs, verified with plutil -lint). Nine behavioral tests against a temp directory: under-cap no rotation, cap crossing rotates once, generations shift + oldest deleted, footprint bound after many rotations, boundary deferral keeps an episode intact, oversized single episode rotates mid-episode, size probed exactly once, pre-existing oversized log discarded not archived, log directory created when missing. No source-text assertions.
6. Validation: CI only. No local xcodebuild on this machine.

Implementation complete. PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/435 (branch c11-220-hang-log-rotation, commit 8da57e3b8). CI is fully green on the first run: build (5m51s, includes the Logic tests gate), compat-tests, remote-daemon-tests, web-typecheck, workflow-guard-tests, build-ghosttykit, and all four drawbridge jobs.

What landed (3 files, +455/-16):
- Sources/MainThreadHangMonitor.swift: new `HangLogRotator` struct plus wiring. appendToLog now delegates to it and takes an episodeBoundary flag; handleRecovery (hang.end) passes true.
- c11Tests/HangLogRotatorTests.swift: 10 behavioral tests, member of c11LogicTests.
- GhosttyTabs.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj: 4 hand-added lines (file ref, build file, group child, c11LogicTests sources entry). plutil -lint OK; CI compiled and ran the file, confirmed in the build log.

Chosen numbers: cap 32 MiB (33554432 bytes, MainThreadHangMonitor.logCapBytes), 2 archived generations (hang.log.1, hang.log.2), soft cap at 75% of the cap. Worst-case footprint ~96 MiB, down from unbounded (the observed 238 MB single-wedge file).

Behavior:
- Size is measured once, lazily, on the first append of the process; thereafter maintained from the offset seekToEnd() already returns. No stat per append.
- Soft cap + episode boundary: a log past 75% rotates only after the closing hang.end record is written, so an episode timeline is never split. Hard cap: a single episode that would push past 32 MiB rotates immediately, mid-episode.
- New file opens with `=== c11 hang.rotated <ts> previous=<name> capBytes=<n> ===`.
- A log that is already over the cap when the rotator first sees it (an older build's uncapped file) is discarded rather than archived, so an oversized file can never sit in the generation set. This means the operator's live ~/Library/Logs/c11/hang.log will be deleted, not archived, on the first hang after upgrade. Manually renamed forensic copies such as hang.log.wedged-20260911 are never touched.
- Nothing throws or traps; a failed archive rename degrades to truncating in place. Runs on the watchdog thread only, after thread_resume; nothing added inside the thread_suspend window. No dlog calls.

Deliberately not done: no local xcodebuild of any scheme (one-build-per-machine rule); no env override for the cap; no cleanup of existing .wedged-* files; no tagged-build smoke launch (the rotator is pure filesystem logic fully covered by the logic suite, and a real 32 MiB stall is not reproducible on demand). PR left open for orchestrator review and merge.

PASS. PR #435 squash-merged; CI fully green on first run including the logic-test gate (10 HangLogRotatorTests). Reviewed by orchestrator: single stat at first append, size tracked from seekToEnd offset, soft cap at episode boundary and hard cap mid-episode, 32 MiB cap with 2 generations, best-effort filesystem calls, discard-over-cap keeps the footprint bound provable.
